lore.title: Sign-in sheet
lore.text: Every line is filled in. The names change; the handwriting does not. At the bottom, in fresh ink: your name, already signed.

lore.title: The ledger
lore.text: Columns: NAME, CARD, NUMBERS CALLED, PRIZE, LEFT AT. The LEFT AT column is empty all the way down, except one entry, which just says 'no'.

lore.title: The ledger, later pages
lore.text: Further back the ledger stops listing bingo and starts listing heroes: classes, levels, how they died. Your parties are in here. So are parties you don't remember playing.

lore.title: Prize counter
lore.text: The prizes are the same every week: a bear, a radio, a ham, a die with no numbers. Nobody has ever claimed the die. The tag says 'reserved'.

lore.title: The cassette
lore.text: A label in careful capitals: CALLING PRACTICE. On it, a voice reads numbers for forty minutes. At the end it says, quietly, 'They liked it better when somebody played back.' Then the campaign rules, read for the first time.

lore.title: The old cage
lore.text: The cage he used to call from. The door is wired shut from the inside. There is a ball still in it. You can't read its number; it keeps rolling away from you.

lore.title: The old cage, again
lore.text: Somebody has cleaned it since you were last here. The ball inside now has a number. It is the number of campaigns you have played.

lore.title: The number board
lore.text: Every number has been called at least once. Except the ones in the bottom corner, which have never lit. The bulbs are fine. He just never calls them.

lore.title: The mask rack
lore.text: A row of painted faces on pegs. Each is a little worn at the mouth. The pegs are labelled in his hand: RECEPTION. PRIZES. NIGHTS. AUCTIONS. KINGS. CHURCH. SHIFTS. UNDERSTUDY. One peg has no label and no mask.

lore.title: The unlabelled peg
lore.text: The empty peg has a mask on it now. It is unfinished: just the outline of a face, and a name you recognise from a hero you lost.

lore.title: Notice board
lore.text: HOUSE RULES: 1. Eyes down. 2. No talking during calls. 3. The caller is always right. 4. The caller may change the house rules. 5. See rule 4. Below: LOST, ONE DIE, TWENTY SIDES, ANSWERS TO NOTHING.

lore.title: A new notice
lore.text: Pinned over the others: CAMPAIGN NIGHT. EVERY NIGHT. ALL WELCOME. ALL STAY. Somebody has crossed out STAY and written WIN. Somebody else has crossed that out.

lore.title: Trophy cabinet
lore.text: Little brass cups for Best Attendance, Most Numbers, Longest Night. The engraving on the newest cup is still being done; you can see the scratches moving.

lore.title: The clock
lore.text: Stopped at seven. Not seven o'clock. Just seven. The second hand twitches every time somebody rolls a die.

lore.title: The exit
lore.text: The sign is lit. The door is real, the handle is real, it opens onto a corridor and the corridor opens onto this hall, from the other end. He doesn't stop you trying.

lore.title: The table
lore.text: The table is older than the hall. Under the felt there are rings from a hundred cups and four initials carved deep into the wood. One set of initials is his. He does not have initials.
